title: Open items closed: 32 tests + CI, and the full 560-item deep scan of Bug Ledger, narrated
summary: The two items left open by the finish pass are done. Bug Ledger now has a 32-test suite (zero dependencies) running in GitHub Actions, guarding the contracts every sweep depends on: scan.mjs --json stays pure JSON, the story renderer resolves found→fixed without mutation, every page's script parses with no duplicate ids, and the admin clustering survives prototype words. Then the full /deepscan ran against the whole ledger — 47 detectors, all 16 bug categories each server-verified N/N, the 67-item security sweep and 117 optimisers — 560/560 confirmed server-side with 62% inspected by detector or code-read, narrated as the second scan story, which now compares itself to the first (16 → 9 real issues). The walk found five real items: a hard-coded scanner date, a click handler stacking on every live re-render, a missing .catch (all fixed), a missing build stamp (recommended) and no global error handler (open — needs a sink). Idempotency keys on the two mutating endpoints are the one recommendation that matters.

Every category ✅ N/N; 66% inspected; 5 real items

metrics.label: Items checked vs the whole ledger
Real defects found by the walk

features: Second scan story with progress vs the first
bugfixes: scan.mjs --write stamped every finding with a constant date
Story page stacked a new click handler on every live re-render (toggles cancelled themselves)
Story load chain had no .catch (endless spinner on a render error)
worklog.mjs header did not document the events command
issues: No global error handler on the pages — needs an error sink first (your call)
POST /api/checks and /api/bugs are not idempotent — retried posts become permanent duplicates (recommended: Idempotency-Key)
findings: A third of the 428 bugs are about surfaces this project does not have; they are grep-verified absent or reasoned, never claimed inspected
The scanner blinds itself on its own repo: its project detectors match the regex sources in scan.mjs, so two of the five real findings were caught by reading, not automation
insights: A test caught a documentation gap within its first run — cheap tests earn their keep immediately
Evidence grading (detector / code-read / reasoned) is what keeps 560/560 honest instead of decorative
